subject: general
question: Himanshi bought a toy for ₹743, decorated it at a cost of ₹8 and sold the toy for ₹750. Find the loss or profit percentage.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total **Cost Price (CP)** = Buying Price + Overhead Expenses = 743 + 8 = 751.

**Selling Price (SP)** = 750.

Since **CP > SP**, there is a **Loss** of 751 − 750 = 1.

Loss% = (Loss ÷ CP) × 100 = (1 ÷ 751) × 100 = 100/751%.

**∴ The correct answer is 100/751% loss.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Purchase Price = 743, Decoration Cost = 8, SP = 750.

**Formulas:** Total CP = Purchase Price + Overhead | Loss = CP − SP | Loss% = (Loss ÷ CP) × 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/73a2e466ddd3e2e6b9c790d0cba6f173392952788b59c79392fe4666a06733c3.png] 

⇒ Total **CP** = 743 + 8 = 751

⇒ **SP** = 750

⇒ **Loss** = 751 − 750 = 1

⇒ **Loss Percentage** = (1 ÷ 751) × 100 = 100/751%

**∴ The correct answer is 100/751% loss.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Effective Cost Price

Any additional expenses like **transportation, repairs, or decoration** incurred after purchasing an article are added to the purchase price to calculate the **Effective Cost Price**.

Profit and Loss Condition

If **SP > CP**, it is a **Profit**. If **CP > SP**, it is a **Loss**. Percentages are always calculated on the **Cost Price (CP)** unless stated otherwise.</p
